claims: Francia was the largest post-Roman Germanic kingdom in Western Europe.
Francia was established by Clovis I in 481 AD.
Francia spanned modern France, Germany, and surrounding areas.
Francia divided into West Francia (France) and East Francia (Germany) in 843.
Francia was founded by Clovis I.
Clovis I united Frankish tribes.
Clovis I expanded into Roman Gaul.
Francia was governed by the Merovingians from 476 to 750.
Francia was governed later by the Carolingians.
Francia reached its height under Charlemagne.
Charlemagne was crowned Emperor in 800.
Francia was divided in 843 by the Treaty of Verdun.
The Treaty of Verdun divided Francia into West Francia ruled by King Charles the Bald, East Francia ruled by King Louis the German, and Middle Francia ruled by Emperor Lothair I.
The Franks adopted Christianity following Clovis I.
The Latin alphabet was used alongside Romance and Germanic languages.
The Carolingian era saw a revival in education and arts.
The Carolingian revival in education and arts occurred particularly under Charlemagne.
Charles Martel won the Battle of Tours in 732.
Francia was originally focused on the region between the Rhine and Seine rivers.
Francia expanded to cover much of Western Europe.
Francia is the direct predecessor to modern France (West Francia).
Francia is the direct predecessor to modern Germany (East Francia).
